newsitem.title: FRANCE: France names mediator for New Caledonia dispute.
newsitem.headline: France names mediator for New Caledonia dispute.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin named a mediator on Wednesday to sort out a controversy over mining rights in New Caledonia that has paralysed negotiations on the future status of the Pacific island.

Jospin named Philippe Essig, a former civil servant and president of state railways operator SNCF, to mediate in the dispute which officials say is key to the political and economic future of the French overseas territory.
At issue are conflicting interests of the French state, New Caledonian Kanak separatists and mining company Eramet, the world's third largest nickel producer.

The French state, which controls 55 percent of Eramet, favours using nickel from one of Eramet's mines to supply a plant that local Kanak company Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) and Canadian Group Falconbridge want to build on the northern part of the island.
The plan was aimed at appeasing the local separatists ahead of a 1998 referendum on independence for the territory.
But Eramet management has opposed any plans that threatened to limit its expansion in New Caledonia, though Eramet shareholders are to choose a new board of directors at a July 31 general meeting.
Jospin, in a letter naming Essig, said his new leftist government favoured construction of a new nickel smelter in northern New Caledonia.
He asked the mediator to evaluate the project's economic and industrial prospects and help facilitate talks between the parties.
